name: during-load-host-profile

base_results.finding: rebuilt validator-4 is correct but v1/v4 ingress delivery remains weak

hypothesis: The item261 delivery skew is caused by host/runtime behavior visible only under load. A during-load profile of the exact item251 binary/config will distinguish CPU saturation, softirq/NIC pressure, socket pressure, and application per-request cost on weak hosts validator-1/validator-4 versus healthy hosts validator-2/validator-3.

samples: process CPU for kombat_chain validator and ingress processes
top kombat_chain thread CPU and CPU core placement
socket summaries and chain port connections

commands: cd chain/deploy/ansible && KOMBAT_PROFILE_DIR=/tmp/and-live-262-profile-100k-60s KOMBAT_PROFILE_SECS=105 KOMBAT_PROFILE_INTERVAL_SECS=2 KOMBAT_OPERATOR_TOKEN=$(grep -m1 '^KOMBAT_OPERATOR_TOKEN=' /tmp/and-live-testnet/validator-1.env | cut -d= -f2-) .venv/bin/ansible-playbook -i inventory/testnet.yml playbooks/capture_load_profile.yml

cd chain/deploy/ansible && KOMBAT_PROFILE_DIR=/tmp/and-live-262-profile2-100k-60s KOMBAT_PROFILE_SECS=105 KOMBAT_PROFILE_INTERVAL_SECS=2 KOMBAT_OPERATOR_TOKEN=$(grep -m1 '^KOMBAT_OPERATOR_TOKEN=' /tmp/and-live-testnet/validator-1.env | cut -d= -f2-) .venv/bin/ansible-playbook -i inventory/testnet.yml playbooks/capture_load_profile.yml
curl kombat_getConsensusMetrics on all four validator RPC endpoints
curl kombat_getStateRootAtHeight at the common height on all four validator RPC endpoints
execution_notes: The first profile run completed at 63,282.4 TPS and captured validator/ingress kombat_chain processes plus host/network counters, but missed remote kombat_loadgen processes. The playbook was fixed and tagged before rerunning.
The second profile run is the decision artifact because it includes kombat_loadgen processes, top processes, and loadgen threads.

result.classification: The corrected profile does not show NIC drops or loadgen saturation on weak hosts. Validator-1 is the clearest weak path: it has much higher request latency (p90 about 204-208ms versus 67-81ms on validators 2/3), lower loadgen CPU, and higher chain CPU per delivered request. Validator-4 is improved after reinstall but still slower than validators 2/3. The skew is application/host runtime latency under load, not packet loss or an exhausted load generator.

decision.reason: The profile explains the item261 skew without changing protocol code. The weak hosts are not failing correctness, dropping packets, or exhausting loadgen CPU; they are slower application/runtime paths under load, especially validator-1. The run improves to 63,823.1 TPS by reusing seeded writers but remains below the 76k green recovery floor.
decision.next_move: Recover green by topology/deployment control, not protocol micro-tuning. Either remove validator-1 from the driven ingress set and replace that ingress capacity with healthier hosts/dedicated load generators, or provision fresh hosts for weak roles and rerun the exact item251 binary/config. Keep the four-validator consensus set unchanged until a codified topology result proves otherwise. Every live performance experiment from here must include a during-load profile artifact, or explicitly state why profiling is not applicable.
